problem: Compute the sum of the first $12$ terms of the geometric series $1+5+25+⋯$

activity_context.topic_title: The Sum of a Finite Geometric Series

feedback.problem: If $k(1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{10})$ is the sum of the first $10$ terms of the geometric series $\frac{4}{3}+\frac{4}{9}+\frac{4}{27}+⋯,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a geometric series, the sum of the first $N$ terms is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term of the series and $r$ is the common ratio.

In our case, ${a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}.$ To find the value of $r,$ we find the ratio of the first two terms in the series:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{(\frac{4}{9})}{(\frac{4}{3})}=\frac{1}{3}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3},N=10$ and $r=\frac{1}{3}$ into our formula, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{10} & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{(1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{10})}{(1-\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{(1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{10})}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{4}{3})}{(\frac{2}{3})}\cdot (1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{10}) \\  & =2\cdot (1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{10})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, comparing the expression above with $k(1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{10}),$ we obtain $k=2.$
